title: Your First Floating Sauna Session
why: First-timers who are curious but unsure: what to pack, how the 1 hour 45 minutes flows, and the river rules, so nerves don't block the booking.
hook_options: Your first floating sauna session, explained
Never done sauna on a river? Start here.
Two towels, a water bottle, and a buddy
caption: First floating sauna session? Pack a swimsuit, two towels, and a non-metal water bottle. Heat in the cedar, cool off in the Columbia or the cold shower, rest on the deck, repeat. The river is real water, so we buddy up and go feet first. The plunge is always optional. #portland #pdx #floatingsauna #coldplunge #saunatime

slides.headline: Your first floating sauna session, explained
slides.body: What to pack, how the 1 hour 45 minutes goes, and the river rules.

slides.headline: Swimsuit. Two towels. A full water bottle.
slides.body: One towel to sit on, one to dry off. Skip metal bottles, they get hot. Arrive hydrated and skip alcohol beforehand.

slides.headline: Heat. Cold. Rest. Repeat.
slides.body: Sweat in the cedar sauna, cool off in the Columbia or the cold shower, then sit on the deck. Go around again.

slides.headline: Is the river safe to plunge?
It's real water. We treat it that way.
slides.body: 40+ feet deep with current. Buddy system, feet first, one at a time, stay within 10 feet. Life jackets and throw rings on board.

slides.headline: When in doubt, don't go out.
slides.body: The river will be there next time. The sauna alone is worth the trip, and the plunge is always optional.

slides.headline: Two towels. Heat, cold, rest. Buddy up.
slides.body: That's it. Social sessions hold up to 8 guests, private sessions up to 10.

slides.headline: Ready for round one?
slides.body: Portland's floating sauna on the Columbia River. Book a session at ebbandember.com.
